Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. As part of our procurement checklist I need a clear mapping of: 1) which marketing cookies/redirection pixels are set by Redwood when customers use the Console and website, 2) what telemetry we collect from the Console (page views, feature flags, usage metrics), and 3) which subprocessors see any of that data and whether transfers to the US occur.

Can you provide a vendor/subprocessor inventory, a brief note on whether any telemetry payloads include PII, and any DPAs or standard contractual clauses that apply? If you have a simple cookie inventory template we can use, please attach.

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Rishi for the procurement thread.

Attached is a lightweight cookie/telemetry inventory template (cookie-inventory-template.xlsx) — please drop any existing vendor info into column B and we’ll fill the rest. Quick answers inline below:

- High level: Redwood does not embed third-party marketing pixels on our hosted Console by default. Marketing pixels are only used on our marketing site (redwood.ai) and require team-level opt-in; we can provide a site-level cookie manifest.
- Console telemetry: anonymized usage events (feature flags, page load timing, API call success/failure counts), aggregate quota metrics, and optional SDK error traces. By design we avoid sending raw customer input to any third-party analytics.
- PII: telemetry payloads do not include free-text customer data. Identifiers are internal IDs and hashed tokens; certain debug traces can include minimally redacted email addresses if a customer enables debug mode (this is off by default).
- Subprocessors: primary analytics/backups/CDN vendors are listed in our subprocessor matrix (see attached). We do use providers with US-hosted infrastructure; however, for EU customers we offer regional tenancy and contractual SCCs/EU Addendum.

Next steps for us: legal to produce subprocessor matrix and DPA pointers; infra to produce a short data-flow diagram for Console telemetry. I’ve attached the cookie inventory template to start.

Can your team fill column B and return by 08/26 so we can hit your 09/03 deadline?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Quick technical summary for the diagram/answers — feel free to paste these into the flow doc: 

- Console telemetry endpoints: telemetry.redwood.ai (EU region endpoints under telemetry.eu.redwood.ai when region=eu), control plane at api.redwood.ai. Events collected: page_view, nav_click, feature_flag, api_latency, sdk_error. Payload fields: event_type, timestamp, client_id (UUID), hashed_user_id (SHA256), feature_name, duration_ms.
- PII: we do not include customer free-text or raw prompts. Debug traces can include partially redacted email addresses if debug=true; debug traces are gated and require explicit customer opt-in.
- Server-side tagging: Redwood does not by default forward telemetry to ad networks. There is no built-in connector to send Console telemetry to marketing/ad vendors. Customers that build server-side integrations using our export APIs can push events to their own tagging stacks — that is customer-managed and outside of Redwood subprocessors.
- Cross-border flows: for Hosted accounts telemetry ingestion may be in the US; for EU region accounts ingestion remains in eu.redwood.ai and backups are regionally isolated. Subprocessors that perform analytics (internal metrics vendor) are contractually bound and listed in the matrix.

If Legal needs specific endpoint IP ranges or signed statements for procurement, I can generate a one-page tech attestation by EOD 08/26.

Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Maya — summary and next steps below (action items for Acme in bold). Thank you for the deadline clarity.

Summary answers:
- Marketing cookies on marketing site only — Console does not load third-party pixels by default.
- Telemetry collected: aggregate usage events, hashed/internal IDs; PII only via explicit debug mode which is disabled by default.
- Subprocessors: see attached matrix; we will export a CSV for procurement if you need.
- Cross-border transfers: Hosted ingestion may be US-based unless you choose EU tenancy; we can sign SCCs and offer regional tenancy for telemetry for Dedicated/Private deals.
- Server-side tagging: no built-in forwarding to ad networks; customers can push data to their own endpoints via our export APIs (customer-controlled).
